claude_content_type.description: Discriminator for a content block. Matches the Anthropic wire format; unknown values deserialize as UNDEFINED and are skipped downstream.

claude_tool_type.description: Discriminator on a tool definition. ABSENT means a caller-executed custom tool -- the only kind that existed before server tools, and the shape every existing caller still sends byte-for-byte. Every value here is an Anthropic-hosted SERVER tool: it runs on Anthropic's infrastructure inside the same request, so there is no tool_use block to answer and no execute callback, and the results come back as content blocks on the same response. The date suffix is the tool VERSION and is part of the wire value; `_20260209` is the dynamic-filtering generation, supported on claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5 (both already in claude_model).

claude_task_budget_type.description: Unit a task budget is denominated in. The API defines exactly one.

claude_service_tier.description: Which tier actually served a request, as reported on every response (verified against api.anthropic.com 2026-08-11: a plain call reports `standard`, a batched one reports `batch`). Load-bearing for cost: a batch reports RAW, undiscounted token counts, so anything pricing a response off token counts alone over-reports a batched call by 2x.

claude_batch_processing_status.description: Lifecycle of a whole batch. `ended` means every request reached a terminal state -- succeeded, errored, canceled or expired -- NOT that they all succeeded.

claude_batch_result_type.description: Terminal state of ONE request inside a batch. Every one of the four is reachable on a batch that ended, so a caller reconciling results has to handle all of them: `expired` in particular is what a request that never ran within 24 hours comes back as.

fields.name: ttl
fields.description: How long an entry written at this breakpoint stays readable: "5m" or "1h". Omitted means the API default of 5 minutes. A string rather than an enum because apibuilder's Scala generator names the case object after the wire value, and neither value is a legal Scala identifier; the type-safe choice lives on AiRequest.cacheTtl instead, which is the surface callers actually use.

claude_tool.description:
A tool the model may call. A single flat model spanning both kinds of tool (discriminated on `type`) rather than a union, for the reason documented on claude_content_block. `type` absent is a CUSTOM tool -- executed by the caller, requiring name + description + input_schema, answered with a tool_result block; that is the only kind that existed before server tools and its wire bytes are unchanged. `type` present is an Anthropic-hosted SERVER tool, which takes name + type and its own options and nothing else.

The two field sets are mutually exclusive on the wire and the API enforces it rather than ignoring the extras: a web_search_20260209 tool carrying a `description` is rejected with `tools.0.web_search_20260209.description: Extra inputs are not permitted` (verified against api.anthropic.com 2026-08-12). That is why description and input_schema are optional here and why callers should build tools through ClaudeTools in lib-ai rather than by hand -- those constructors are what make the two shapes unmixable.

Populated by kind: custom -> name, description, input_schema, strict; web_search_20260209 -> name, type, max_uses, allowed_domains/blocked_domains; web_fetch_20260209 -> name, type, max_uses, allowed_domains/blocked_domains, citations, max_content_tokens.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Custom: the name the model calls. Server: the fixed name the API defines for that tool -- `web_search` and `web_fetch` respectively. Sending anything else is rejected.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Absent for a custom tool. See claude_tool_type.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Custom tools only. What the tool does and when to call it -- the model picks tools from this, so be prescriptive about WHEN, not just what. Rejected on a server tool.

fields.name: input_schema
fields.description: Custom tools only. JSON schema for the tool's arguments. Rejected on a server tool, which has a schema the API already knows.

fields.name: max_uses
fields.description: Server tools only. Cap on how many times the model may invoke this tool within one request. Exceeding it does NOT fail the request: the tool result block comes back with an error object naming `max_uses_exceeded` -- see claude_server_tool_error.

fields.name: allowed_domains
fields.description: Server tools only. Restricts the tool to these domains. Mutually exclusive with blocked_domains.

fields.name: blocked_domains
fields.description: Server tools only. Excludes these domains. Mutually exclusive with allowed_domains.

fields.name: citations
fields.description: web_fetch only. Whether fetched content is cited in the answer.

fields.name: max_content_tokens
fields.description: web_fetch only. Truncates fetched page content to this many tokens before it enters the context window -- the lever for a fetch of an unbounded page not eating the whole budget.

claude_web_search_result.description: One hit inside a web_search_tool_result block's content array. `encrypted_content` is opaque and must be echoed back verbatim when the block is replayed on a later turn -- it is how the API restores the fetched page without re-fetching it.

claude_web_fetch_result.description: The content of a web_fetch_tool_result block -- a single object, NOT a list (unlike web search). `content` is the fetched page as a `document` content block; it is left as raw json here because its shape is the Files/document surface rather than anything this client constructs.

claude_server_tool_error.description: A server tool that FAILED. This is the trap the whole decoding surface exists for: the request is an ordinary HTTP 200, the block is an ordinary web_search_tool_result / web_fetch_tool_result, and only its `content` differs -- a single error OBJECT where a success carries a list (web search) or a result object (web fetch). Anything that reaches into content positionally throws on exactly the cases that matter: max_uses_exceeded, a blocked domain, an unavailable page. Decode through ClaudeServerToolResults in lib-ai, which returns the error rather than throwing on it.

fields.name: error_code
fields.description: e.g. `max_uses_exceeded`, `too_many_requests`, `unavailable`, `invalid_input`. An open set -- treat an unrecognized code as a failure, not as an impossibility.

claude_output_config.description: Output controls. effort tunes thinking depth and token spend; format constrains the response to a JSON schema (replaces the deprecated top-level output_format); task_budget tells the model how much of max_tokens it should plan to spend.

claude_task_budget.description: Advisory token ceiling the model is made aware of while generating. The server injects a countdown marker, so the model paces itself and wraps up gracefully instead of being truncated at max_tokens -- which is an enforced ceiling the model never sees. Requires the task-budgets-2026-03-13 beta header.

fields.name: total
fields.description: Tokens the model may plan to spend on this turn. Minimum accepted by the API is 20,000; anything lower is rejected.

claude_api_output_format.description: Structured output configuration for guaranteed JSON schema compliance

fields.name: schema
fields.description: JSON schema object defining the structure

claude_content_block.description: One content block on a message or response. A single flat model spanning all block types (discriminated on type) rather than a union, because a spec that has both a union and error-response mustParse handling hits a known bryzek-generator ambiguous-implicit compile error. Wire JSON is identical to the union form; only the populated fields differ by type: text -> text; tool_use -> id, name, input; tool_result -> tool_use_id, content, is_error; thinking -> thinking, signature; redacted_thinking -> data; image -> source; document -> source; server_tool_use -> id, name, input; web_search_tool_result / web_fetch_tool_result / code_execution_tool_result -> tool_use_id, content. Retain every field verbatim when echoing assistant content back, or the API rejects the modified block.

fields.name: content
fields.description: Raw json rather than a string because the wire type genuinely varies by block type and the API sends all three shapes: a STRING on a tool_result this client writes, an ARRAY of claude_web_search_result on a web_search_tool_result, and an OBJECT on a web_fetch_tool_result (claude_web_fetch_result), a code_execution_tool_result, or ANY server tool result that errored (claude_server_tool_error). Typed as string -- as it was before server tools -- the readNullable[String] fails and the WHOLE response is unparseable the moment a search runs, not just the one block. Write it with ClaudeClient.toolResultBlock and read it with ClaudeServerToolResults; do not reach into it positionally.

fields.name: server_tool_use
fields.description: How many times each Anthropic-hosted tool ran. Load-bearing for cost in the same way service_tier is: web search is billed PER REQUEST ($10 per 1,000) on top of tokens, so anything pricing a response off token counts alone under-reports every request that searched.

fields.name: service_tier
fields.description: Tier that served this request. Optional only because a response recorded before this field existed does not carry one; the live API sets it on every response. Anything computing cost MUST read it -- see claude_service_tier.

claude_cache_creation.description: cache_creation_input_tokens split by the TTL each write was made at. Without this split a 1h write (2x input) is indistinguishable from a 5m one (1.25x) and any cost rollup over the total under-reports it -- which is exactly the direction that would hide a longer TTL that stopped paying for itself.

claude_server_tool_usage.description: Per-tool invocation counts on one response. Defaulted to 0 rather than optional: a response that ran no server tool omits the field entirely, and `0 searches` is the honest reading of that, not `unknown`.

claude_batch_form.description: Body of a batch submission. The API caps a batch at 100,000 requests or 256 MB, whichever comes first.

claude_batch_request_item.description: One request in a batch. `custom_id` is the ONLY way a result is matched back to its caller: results are returned in ARBITRARY order (verified 2026-08-11 -- a batch submitted a, b, c came back c, b, a), so never key by position. `params` is a full Messages request, minus the two things a batch rejects: `fallbacks` and fast mode.

claude_batch_request_counts.description: How the batch's requests are distributed across terminal states. While processing_status is in_progress these move; once it is ended, `processing` is 0 and the rest sum to the batch size.

claude_batch.description: A submitted batch. `results_url` is null until processing_status is `ended`; asking for results before then is an error, not an empty list.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: 24 hours after creation. Anything still processing at this point comes back as an `expired` result -- the hard ceiling on batch latency.

claude_batch_result.description: One line of the JSONL results body -- see claude_batch_result_detail for why this is not fetched through the generated client.

claude_batch_result_detail.description: Outcome of one request. A flat model discriminated on `type` rather than a union, for the reason documented on claude_content_block. Populated by type: succeeded -> message; errored -> error; canceled and expired populate NEITHER, so a caller that reads `message.get` on anything but `succeeded` will throw on the two states that mean the batch ran out of time or was called off.

claude_batch.description: The Message Batches API: the same Messages surface at 50% of the token price, run asynchronously. Three of its four operations are ordinary JSON and generated here. The fourth -- GET /v1/messages/batches/:id/results, which carries the actual payload -- returns `application/x-jsonl` rather than JSON, which apibuilder has no response type for, so it is fetched by hand (see ClaudeBatchResults in lib-ai) and its lines parsed as claude_batch_result.

operations.description: Best-effort cancellation. Requests already in flight are allowed to finish, so a canceled batch generally ends with a mix of `succeeded` and `canceled` results rather than all `canceled`.
